content.title: About
content.content: Corn tortillas are thin flatbreads made from whole‑grain corn flour, water and salt. They are shelf‑stable and can be kept at room temperature for several months. The tortillas have a soft, slightly sweet corn flavor and are extremely versatile in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn tortillas originate from traditional Mexican cuisine and have been used since pre‑colonial times.
The dough is traditionally prepared by nixtamalization, soaking corn kernels in an alkaline lime solution, which increases nutrient bioavailability.
Corn tortillas are naturally gluten‑free, making them suitable for people with celiac disease.
Unlike wheat tortillas, corn tortillas stay crisp when fried, forming a golden crust.
Shelf‑stable versions are packaged in moisture‑proof wrappers to extend shelf life.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Corn flour provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Tortillas deliver slow‑releasing energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6 and magnesium
items.content: These micronutrients are involved in protein metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Ideal for those following a gluten‑free diet or with gluten intolerance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Corn tortillas contain virtually no fat, making them a light base for many dishes.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain tortilla varieties contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you need to limit sodium intake.

items.title: Texture loss if stored improperly
items.content: Exposure to moisture can make tortillas soft and cause them to lose their structure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use corn tortillas for tacos, burritos, quesadillas, chips, or as a base for casseroles. They can be quickly warmed on a dry skillet, in the microwave, or in the oven. For extra crispness, lightly fry them in a small amount of oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep tortillas in their original sealed package in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer to an airtight bag or container to prevent moisture absorption. Properly stored, they remain good for 6‑12 months.
